name: Ella Core
what_it_is: A production-oriented open-source 5G core network packaged as a single binary with an embedded database and eBPF-based data plane, designed for private network deployments in factories, warehouses, stadiums, ships, and remote sites. It consolidates all 5G core network functions into one process with a built-in web UI and REST API.
components: AMF (Access and Mobility Management Function) — handles NAS and NGAP
SMF (Session Management Function) — manages PDU sessions via PFCP
UPF (User Plane Function) — eBPF/XDP data plane, 10+ Gbps, <1ms latency
UDM/UDR — subscriber data management with embedded SQLite database
NRF — network function registration and discovery
REST API server on port 5002 with OpenAPI spec and Go client
Web UI — subscriber, radio, network, and policy management
OpenTelemetry collector integration for traces, metrics, logs, profiles
protocols: NAS (Non-Access Stratum) — UE registration and session management signaling
NGAP (N2 interface) — gNB control plane over SCTP, default port 38412
GTP-U (N3 interface) — user plane encapsulation between gNB and UPF
SBI (Service-Based Interface) — internal NF communication over HTTP/2
measurement: OpenTelemetry traces via OTLP (configurable endpoint, default localhost:4317)
System log with configurable level (debug/info/warn/error) and output
Real-time flow monitoring and usage reports via web UI
Grafana dashboards shipped in repo (grafana/ directory)
configuration: Single YAML file (core.yaml); only file path passed via --config flag
logging.system.level: debug|info|warn|error; output: stdout or file path
db.path: path to embedded SQLite database file
interfaces.n3.name: network interface name for GTP-U (N3)
interfaces.n6.name: network interface name for external data network (N6)
xdp.attach-mode: generic|native|offload — eBPF XDP attachment mode
modes: xdp.attach-mode generic — software XDP, works on all NICs including virtual/container interfaces
xdp.attach-mode native — kernel driver XDP, requires driver support
xdp.attach-mode offload — NIC hardware offload XDP
constraints: Requires Linux with eBPF/XDP support; not portable to non-Linux hosts
Container must run privileged (privileged: true) for eBPF and network namespace access
N6 network must NOT be Docker-internal — UE packets are dropped on internal networks
Minimum hardware: 1 CPU core, 1 GB RAM, 10 GB disk
Single-binary single-process architecture — no horizontal scaling or HA mode documented
No built-in fault injection capability; no chaos/failure simulation tooling in repo
docker_services: ella-core — image ella-core:latest; ports 5002:5002; privileged; networks: default (eth0), n3 (10.3.0.2), n6 (10.6.0.2)
ueransim — image ghcr.io/ellanetworks/ueransim:3.2.7; gNB + UE simulator; privileged; networks: default, n3 (10.3.0.3)
ella-core-tester — image ghcr.io/ellanetworks/ella-core-tester (digest-pinned); raw N3 test node at 10.3.0.3/10.3.0.4; privileged
router — image ghcr.io/ellanetworks/ubuntu-router:0.1; adds route 10.45.0.0/22 via N6; runs responder.py on port 34242; networks: n6 (10.6.0.3)
n3 network — internal Docker bridge, subnet 10.3.0.0/24
n6 network — external-capable Docker bridge, subnet 10.6.0.0/24
notable_absences: No fault injection or chaos engineering tooling
No Kubernetes-native operator (k8s/ directory exists but contains raw manifests only)
No PCAP or packet capture integration built in
No rate limiting or QoS policy enforcement visible in config schema
No TLS configuration for the REST API or SBI interfaces in the config file
